subject: English
passage:
The following text is adapted from a 1920 short story about small-town life.

It is a common observation in the village of Millbrook that Mrs. Weatherby keeps more personal affairs locked away than the town banker keeps money.

Mrs. Weatherby's leather satchel is, fittingly, extraordinarily secure, fastened with multiple clasps and wrapped with a cord that seems to have been tied and retied countless times, giving it a weathered appearance, as if it has been through many seasons of careful handling. When Mrs. Weatherby opens her satchel for business, the personal affairs do not spill out like autumn leaves, but remain carefully filed away beneath layers of organized compartments.
prompt: Based on the text, how do people in Millbrook most likely regard Mrs. Weatherby?

choices.A: Many have grown weary of her overly cautious handling of documents.
choices.B: Some disapprove of how openly she shares details about her own life.
choices.C: Most would think poorly of her if not for her organizational abilities.
choices.D: Few worry that she will reveal their private matters.

explanation: Choice D is the best answer. The text describes a common observation that Weatherby keeps more personal affairs locked away than a banker keeps money. It also says that when she opens her satchel, 'the personal affairs do not spill out… but remain carefully filed away,' suggesting that she will not reveal private matters.
